summary: The Cursed Lands, the veiled valley: a hidden people, the barrows and what the mounds keep, strangers at the edge and the night the dead walk.

the_veil_spirit.name: The Veil
the_veil_spirit.desc: A veil of stone, custom and something no traveller could name.

the_veil_2.name: A People Apart
the_veil_2.desc: The veil is drawn tighter, and nothing else is anyone's business.

edge_watchers.name: Watchers at the Edge
edge_watchers.desc: Hooded watchers at the border stone, in the same places as their grandmothers.

barrow_lanterns.name: Lanterns on the Mounds
barrow_lanterns.desc: Lit at dusk, burning until dawn, every night since before any record.

barrow_lanterns_2.name: The Mounds Are Quiet
barrow_lanterns_2.desc: The keepers have pronounced the mounds quiet, and the valley holds its breath.

terraces.name: Terraced Fields
terraces.desc: Every slope terraced to the very top, and nothing wasted.

self_sufficient.name: Enough for Ourselves
self_sufficient.desc: The valley feeds, clothes and arms itself, and buys nothing.

crack_in_the_veil.name: A Crack in the Veil
crack_in_the_veil.desc: A few strangers admitted, a few of the valley folk sent out.

the_dead_walk.name: When the Dead Walk
the_dead_walk.desc: The lanterns on the mounds gutter and flare.

the_old_tallies.title: The Old Tallies
the_old_tallies.desc: The Tally-Keeper counts what the mounds keep, as every year, on knotted cords in the lantern-light. He does not say what the cords add up to, and no one in the valley has ever thought to ask him.

veiled_envoys.title: Veiled Envoys
veiled_envoys.desc: Hooded envoys of the Cursed Lands have come to the moot of the Red Woods with fruit and a few plain words. They ask only that the forest and the valley leave each other be, and they wait to hear the answer.

tax_men_at_the_edge.title: Tax-Men at the Edge
tax_men_at_the_edge.desc: A party of Parim's tax-men has reached the border stone, courteous, persistent and entirely lost. The watchers could turn them back, or they could pay a small token to be left in peace.

a_scholar_asks.title: A Scholar Asks
a_scholar_asks.desc: A scholar of the Lost Cause stands at the border stone and asks, very politely, to read the tallies of the barrows. The Elder is told, and the watchers wait for a nod, a pause or an empty chair.

almoners_at_the_edge.title: Almoners at the Edge
almoners_at_the_edge.desc: Almoners of the Deliverer wait at the border stone with bread, linen and a plan for a hospital in the valley. The watchers send word to the Elder, who is patient, and so are they.

focuses.name: The Veil
focuses.desc: The Cursed Lands lie behind a veil that is partly stone, partly custom and partly something no traveller has ever been able to name. Parim calls the land cursed; its people do not say why.

focuses.name: No Road In
focuses.desc: The valley roads are closed with stone and thorn, and the passes are narrowed to a footpath. Anyone who wishes to enter must first be seen to have a reason.

focuses.name: The Elder's Silence
focuses.desc: The Veiled Elder governs the valley and says very little. A decision from the Elder is a nod, a pause or an empty chair, and the valley has always understood which is which.

focuses.name: Watchers at the Edge
focuses.desc: Hooded watchers stand at the valley's edge, in the same places their grandmothers stood. They wave no one in, and they wave no one off.

focuses.name: The Unspoken Law
focuses.desc: There is a law in the valley that is never written and never spoken, and no one has ever been found who broke it twice.

focuses.name: A People Apart
focuses.desc: The valley folk agree that they are a people apart, and the veil is drawn tighter. They want to be left alone, and nothing else about them is anyone's business.

focuses.name: The Veil Holds
focuses.desc: The veil has held for longer than the Concord has stood. It will go on holding, so long as no one looks too closely at what it is made of.

focuses.name: The Barrow-Keepers
focuses.desc: The valley keeps barrows older than the Concord, and a line of keepers older than the barrows. They speak of them as the mounds, and of what the mounds keep as nothing in particular.

focuses.name: Lanterns on the Mounds
focuses.desc: Lanterns are lit on the mounds at dusk and kept burning until dawn. They have been lit every night since before any record, and the tallow is never allowed to run low.

focuses.name: The Old Tallies
focuses.desc: The Tally-Keeper counts what the mounds keep, as every year. The count is written on knotted cords, and nobody outside the valley has ever seen one.

focuses.name: Quiet Earth
focuses.desc: The earth over the mounds is kept still: no plough, no spade, no wandering goat. The keepers say a quiet earth is a quiet sleep.

focuses.name: The Keepers' Oath
focuses.desc: Each keeper swears an oath that is spoken only once, in the dark, at the foot of the oldest mound. What it says is not known beyond the valley, and not all of it within.

focuses.name: The Mounds Are Quiet
focuses.desc: The keepers pronounce the mounds quiet, and a hush falls on the valley. It is a hush of the kind one hears before a storm, or after one.

focuses.name: The Hidden Valley
focuses.desc: The valley is hidden from every road, and its one pass is a goat-track under an overhang. Inside, the land is green and well-tended, and quiet as a held breath.

focuses.name: Terraced Fields
focuses.desc: The valley's slopes are terraced to the very top, each wall dry-laid and mended every spring. Nothing is wasted, and nothing is sold.

focuses.name: Charcoal and Iron
focuses.desc: Charcoal-burners and smelters work in a hidden gully, their smoke drawn away down a long flue so that no stranger will ever see it.

focuses.name: The Inner Smithy
focuses.desc: The valley's smiths work behind closed doors, and the work that leaves their forge is never marked. Their blades are plain and extremely sharp.

focuses.name: Enough for Ourselves
focuses.desc: The valley feeds, clothes and arms itself. It buys nothing and sells nothing, and the valley folk are well content to keep it that way.

focuses.name: Strangers at the Edge
focuses.desc: Strangers arrive at the edge, usually one at a time, usually hungry. The watchers meet each at the border stone and hear what they have to say.

focuses.name: Words with the Redbarks
focuses.desc: The red-barked tribes of the northern forest are the valley's neighbours and have never asked to enter. The Elder sends a messenger with fruit and a few plain words.

focuses.name: The Tax-Men Turned Back
focuses.desc: Parim's tax-men have reached the edge of the valley with their ledgers and their escorts. They are courteous, they are persistent, and they have not understood where they are.

focuses.name: A Scholar at the Edge
focuses.desc: A scholar of the Lost Cause has walked a long way to ask a question. The watchers hear it, and send word to the Elder, who does not answer.

focuses.name: Healers from Outside
focuses.desc: Almoners of the Deliverer come to the edge with bread and medicine and a plan for a hospital. The watchers send them back to the border stone and tell them to wait.

focuses.name: A Crack in the Veil
focuses.desc: A few strangers are admitted to the valley, and a few of the valley folk are sent out in return. The veil is not lifted, only thinned, and the Elder says nothing at all.

focuses.name: When the Dead Walk
focuses.desc: The lanterns on the mounds gutter and flare. Whatever the barrows keep, the dead have begun to walk elsewhere, and the valley must choose what it will do about it.

focuses.name: Bar the Barrows
focuses.desc: Every barrow is sealed with stone and thorn, and the keepers take their stations on the mounds. The veil is drawn tight, and what the mounds keep will keep.

focuses.name: Open the Veil
focuses.desc: The Elder lifts the veil. The valley folk go out among the living, with their bows and their silence, and the living find that they are very good company in a dark hour.

focuses.name: The Long Night Watch
focuses.desc: The watchers are doubled and then doubled again. They stand through the long nights with lanterns and bows, and they do not talk about what they are watching for.

focuses.name: With the Living
focuses.desc: The valley folk come out in their dark cloaks to stand with the Heir. They ask for nothing, and they say very little, and they fight as if they had been waiting for this all their lives.

focuses.name: The Veil Mended
focuses.desc: The war is over, and the Elder draws the veil closed once more. Whatever came out has gone back in, and the lanterns on the mounds burn steady again.
